items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: And Grady was still playing, and Frank was playing too, behind him.

ctx.x: Yeah he couldn’t come out and say look, you’ve got to take care of these guys, you can’t just have us play all the time like that and don’t take care of us. And one by one they just sneaked away. I mean I can imagine that happening. There’s a funny story, and I hope it doesn’t hurt anybody’s feelings. But once I was working with Lionel Hampton. We had

taken a gig with him at Rodney Dangerfield’s place in New York. I had a group called the New York Jazz Quartet at that time. And Hamp loved it. And I loved him, I always have loved him. But whenever we’d play together he would play, he’d never stop playing. He would never stop playing. So finally one day I said to Frank [Wess], I says, “Frank, I don’t want to hurt his feelings, but how can we get him to know when the time is up? How can we get him to know that hey, we’ve played an hour and a half, and he wants to…
Right. That’s funny. Did he get out of it gracefully?
